entries.06a8b42d33272081: This reporting segment handles exploration, prospecting and development of oil, natural gas and other mineral and energy resources, extraction, processing, storage, sale and purchase, and transportation of by-products, and the capture, transportation, storage and use of carbon dioxide, and is carried out by ENEOS Xplora Corporation. The company changed its name from JX Oil & Energy Exploration Corporation in January 2025. The company describes this subsidiary as a company that, in addition to oil and natural gas development, production and sales, also engages in environmentally responsive businesses centered on CCS/CCUS (carbon dioxide capture and storage / carbon dioxide capture, utilization and storage). Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥216,744 million; revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥216,747 million (down 10.7% year on year), and segment profit was ¥50,833 million (down ¥36.6 billion year on year). The company explains that revenue and profit declined because, although crude oil and natural gas production increased due to factors such as a higher participating interest following the conclusion of a new production sharing contract for Block 15-2 off Vietnam and increased production from Middle East projects, production volume that can be received as investment recovery under the production sharing contract for Block SK10 off Sarawak, Malaysia decreased after one-time investment in the previous period was completed, and selling prices fell in line with market conditions. Segment assets were ¥1,294,205 million, the second largest among Petroleum Products and Others, the number of employees was 1,203, and capital expenditure was ¥52,690 million for exploration and development investment in oil and gas fields. For Block SK10 off Sarawak, Malaysia, in which the company acquired an interest in 1987, the company concluded in June 2025 a contract with PETRONAS, the state-owned national energy company of Malaysia, extending the production sharing contract by 10 years, from 2028 to 2038. In CCS/CCUS, the company is promoting the Petra Nova CCUS Project in the United States. As an adjacent area, it is also working on the development of rare resources using underground technology cultivated through oil and natural gas development and production. In addition to its helium business already entered in Canada, the company decided to invest in Gold Hydrogen, an exploration and development company for natural hydrogen and helium based in Australia. As of April 1, 2026, the natural gas business of ENEOS Corporation has been transferred to and integrated into ENEOS Xplora, establishing a system that operates in an integrated manner from upstream to downstream.

entries.3c62ae664545abbf: A reportable segment handling petroleum refining and sales, basic chemicals, lubricants, gas and hydrogen, centered on ENEOS Corporation. The company describes it as a company that, in addition to its petroleum refining and sales business, which has Japan's largest share of fuel oil sales, also works on next-generation energy businesses such as SAF (sustainable aviation fuel), hydrogen and synthetic fuels as part of efforts to realize energy transition. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥10,341,787 million, accounting for 88% of consolidated revenue of ¥11,765,470 million; revenue including intersegment revenue was ¥10,395,319 million (down 5.3% year on year). Segment profit (presented as operating income or loss in the consolidated statement of income) was ¥292,362 million, an increase of ¥343.1 billion year on year; in the prior year it was a loss of ¥50,705 million. The company states that this profit includes an accounting loss of ¥7.8 billion from inventory effects (the prior-year period had a loss of ¥57.6 billion), and that operating profit excluding inventory effects was ¥300.2 billion, an increase of ¥293.3 billion year on year. Segment assets were ¥5,938,078 million, segment liabilities ¥4,010,046 million, depreciation and amortization ¥209,097 million, impairment losses ¥26,877 million, and the number of employees was 20,108 (excluding 12,082 temporary employees); capital expenditure was ¥192,819 million, mainly for facility construction at refineries and plants and the construction and renovation of service stations (SS). It states that it aims to achieve an operating rate of 90% excluding regular maintenance in fiscal 2027. In the current period, the shipping business of ENEOS Ocean Corporation other than its crude oil tanker business was succeeded by the newly established NYK Energy Ocean Corporation through an absorption-type company split, and a gain on sale arose from the transfer of 80% of its shares to Nippon Yusen Kabushiki Kaisha.

entries.6e1818340be910bf: ENEOS Holdings, Inc. is a holding company, and the corporate group consists of the company, 476 subsidiaries, and 149 companies accounted for by the equity method and others. The reportable segments are the 5 segments of 'Petroleum Products and Other,' 'Oil and Natural Gas Exploration and Production,' 'Functional Materials,' 'Electricity,' and 'Renewable Energy,' and businesses not included in the reportable segments are grouped into the 'Other' category. Oil is at the center of the business, and revenue from external customers in the Petroleum Products and Other segment of ¥10,341,787 million in the fiscal year ended March 2026 accounts for 88% of consolidated revenue of ¥11,765,470 million. The core flow is importing crude oil, refining it at refineries, and making and selling fuel oils such as gasoline and diesel oil as well as basic chemicals and lubricants, and branching off from this are upstream oil and natural gas exploration and production (ENEOS Xplora Corporation), downstream electricity and city gas (ENEOS Power Corporation), functional materials for chemicals (ENEOS Materials Corporation), and renewable energy (ENEOS Renewable Energy Corporation). Business results are greatly affected by 2 figures that the company cannot decide itself. Crude oil prices (Dubai crude) in the fiscal year ended March 2026 began at $76 for 1 barrel at the start of the period, remained weak throughout the year affected by demand trends in Asia and production adjustments by OPEC Plus and other factors, but surged at the end of the period to $121 against the background of heightened tensions in the Middle East in March, and the period average was $72, $7 lower than the same period of the previous year. The yen's exchange rate against the U.S. dollar began at ¥150 at the start of the period, the yen temporarily appreciated to the early ¥140 range in mid-April, then moved on a yen-depreciation trend and reached ¥160 at the end of the period, and the period average was ¥151, with the yen appreciating by ¥2 from the same period of the previous year. Another factor that moves an oil company's profits is the inventory effect (the effect on cost of sales of the valuation of inventories by the gross average method and write-downs of book value), and the company puts the equivalent of operating profit excluding the inventory effect at ¥474,400 million, against operating profit of ¥466,600 million. The breakdown of revenue by region (based on the location of customers) is Japan ¥8,789,295 million, Singapore ¥984,106 million, China ¥553,434 million, and Other ¥1,438,635 million, and there is no external customer accounting for more than 10% of revenue. The company formulated the 4th Medium-Term Management Plan (fiscal 2025-2027) in May 2025, with 'transformation to a lean management structure' and 'portfolio restructuring' as its 2 pillars. Under the former, through intra-group reorganization aimed at selling non-core businesses and eliminating duplication of organizations and functions, the company reduced the number of consolidated companies by 13 from the end of March 2025, and has formulated a plan to reduce the number by about 100 companies compared with the end of March 2025. It has also established a dedicated organization, the 'AI Innovation Department,' and is building a system to centrally manage and use data across the entire supply chain, from crude oil procurement to manufacturing, logistics, and sales. Under the latter, in March 2025, on the new listing of JX Advanced Metals Corporation, the company sold a portion of its shares and made the company an equity-method affiliate, and in May 2026 it decided to acquire the oil refining and sales business that Chevron operates in Southeast Asia and Australia. The company states that while a structural decline in oil demand is expected in Japan, growth in demand over the medium to long term is expected in Southeast Asia and Australia, and that it aims, through this acquisition, to greatly expand overseas revenue and increase it to a scale of about 50% in fiscal 2030. In terms of funding, it flexibly chooses direct financing such as commercial paper and corporate bonds and indirect financing such as borrowings from financial institutions, and also uses sustainable finance such as institutional loans for crude oil stockpiling funds and transition-linked loans. The maximum amount of the specified financing facility agreement (commitment line agreement) at the end of the current consolidated fiscal year is ¥227,500 million, and there is no borrowing balance under the agreement.

entries.bc340487e834846a: This reporting segment handles power generation, electricity procurement and sales, city gas, overseas renewable energy, and VPP (virtual power plant), and is carried out by ENEOS Power Corporation. In April 2024, the company succeeded to the electricity and city gas business of ENEOS Corporation through an absorption-type company split. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥332,198 million; revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥349,219 million (up 9.2% year on year), and segment profit was ¥21,996 million (up ¥1.0 billion year on year). The company explains that profit increased despite the reversal of one-time profit recorded in the previous period and the impact of impairment losses, due to the full operation of the Goi Thermal Power Station and an increase in retail sales volume, among other factors. The impairment loss for the period was ¥8,047 million. Segment assets were ¥248,997 million, and the number of employees was 319, the smallest among the reporting segments. Capital expenditure was ¥5,614 million for construction work on new power generation facilities. Based on its equity interest as of March 31, 2026, the power generation capacity (excluding power sources under construction) is approximately 2.2 million kW. As of April 1, 2026, the electricity business and the renewable energy business have shifted to a substantively integrated management structure, with officers holding concurrent positions and parts of the organization operated as one.

entries.c770fa2fe23a76f7: This business refines crude oil at refineries and produces and sells fuel oils such as gasoline and diesel. Sales volume for the fiscal year ended March 2026 rose 2.7% year on year, which the company attributes to an increase in export volumes following refinery operating conditions, while domestic demand for petroleum products continued to decline structurally, mainly due to improved fuel efficiency of automobiles, and it thoroughly pursued profitable sales. The company states that, while fulfilling its responsibility for the stable supply of petroleum products in Japan, it sought to improve earnings through flexible product export responses according to overseas market conditions. By advancing improvements in the accuracy of equipment assessment and in operational efficiency to develop an environment for engineers, it established the “E-MORE Project Office” as a dedicated organization to promote fundamental reform of maintenance operations through AI and DX. Amid heightened tensions in the Middle East, uncertainty over crude oil supply has increased, and the company states that to maintain stable supply of petroleum products it is using national stockpiles, diversifying suppliers, and urgently procuring crude oil and petroleum products from the market. In May 2026, to expand its overseas fuel oil business, it decided to acquire the petroleum refining and sales business that Chevron operates in Southeast Asia and Australia (6 countries: Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, Australia, Vietnam and Indonesia), and states that in Singapore it will acquire a 50% interest in Singapore Refining Company, which owns a refinery.

In biofuels, the company is preparing to establish a mass-production supply system aiming to produce 400,000 KL per year of SAF (Sustainable Aviation Fuel) at the Wakayama Plant from fiscal 2028 onward. In April 2025, the company decided to invest in UK-based C2X to build a green methanol supply chain and link it to the business development of production and sales, and the company states that through this investment it is considering building a supply chain for the shipping sector and expanding into synthetic fuels and chemicals using biomass feedstocks. In July 2025, the company decided to participate in the biofuel production and sales business at the Kapolei Refinery in Hawaii, United States, promoted by US-based Par Pacific.
entries.dac67cd69f9fe125: In April 2017, JX Holdings, Inc. made TonenGeneral Sekiyu K.K. a wholly owned subsidiary through a share exchange, and then JX Energy Corporation absorbed and merged TonenGeneral Sekiyu K.K., after which JX Holdings, Inc. succeeded, through an absorption-type company split, to part of the rights and obligations that JX Energy Corporation had succeeded to from TonenGeneral Sekiyu K.K. Together with this, JX Holdings, Inc. changed its trade name to JXTG Holdings, Inc. and JX Energy Corporation changed its trade name to JXTG Energy Corporation. The TonenGeneral Group began in May 1893 with the opening of the Japanese branches of Socony (Standard Oil Company of New York) of the United States and Vacuum Oil of the United States, and TonenGeneral Sekiyu K.K. was formed in July 2000 by the merger of Toa Nenryo Kogyo K.K., established in July 1939 (its trade name was changed to Tonen Corporation in July 1989), and General Bussan K.K., established in July 1947 (its trade name was changed to General Sekiyu K.K. in January 1967), and it merged with EMG Marketing G.K. in January 2017.
entries.de7c61ae9fe986bb: This is a power generation business centered on thermal power generation. The Goi Thermal Power Station, which began full operation in March 2025, is in place, and the company states that it maximized its supply capacity in the fiscal year ended March 2026 to strengthen electricity sales and achieve improved earnings. Based on its equity interest as of March 31, 2026, the power generation capacity of the electricity segment (excluding power sources under construction) is approximately 2.2 million kW. To achieve stabilization of earnings, the company is promoting risk hedging using electricity futures to avoid volatility risk in the wholesale electricity market, and the company states that this is steadily producing results.

entries.df186b31ec62244c: On March 19, 2025, JX Metals Corporation, which had been a subsidiary of the company, was newly listed on the Prime Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Because the company sold part of the shares of that company it held in connection with the listing, the company's ownership ratio after the offering became 42.4%, it lost control, and that company changed from a subsidiary to an equity-method affiliate. In connection with this, the company classified the metals business, consisting of JX Metals and its subsidiaries and others, as a discontinued operation and changed the classification of its reportable segments. Profit for the period from discontinued operations of ¥229,569 million includes ¥153,334 million of gains related to the sale arising from the loss of control. The company positions this as part of the "portfolio restructuring," a pillar of its 4th Medium-Term Management Plan.
entries.e64b6fe8cd888ffd: This is the starting point of the metals business and the lineage of JX Metals Corporation, which became an equity-method affiliate in March 2025. The business that began with a copper mine became another pillar alongside oil, and it left the subsidiaries upon its listing in 2025. In the segment information for the fiscal year ended March 2026, the metals business is included in the "Other" category as equity in earnings of JX Metals accounted for by the equity method, and the ¥405,493 million of investments accounted for by the equity method is also mainly the amount related to investment in that company.
entries.e73a906aeffaff11: This reporting segment handles synthetic rubber, specialty synthetic rubber, secondary battery materials, emulsions, thermoplastic elastomers, high-performance monomers, and high-performance polymers, and is carried out by ENEOS Materials Corporation. The company describes this subsidiary as a company engaged in the production and sale of synthetic rubber and related products used mainly as tire materials, as well as high-performance chemical products. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥336,507 million, the second largest among the reporting segments after Petroleum Products and Others; revenue including intersegment transactions was ¥338,988 million (down 2.3% year on year), and segment profit was ¥11,076 million (down ¥6.6 billion year on year). The company explains that profit declined because, although sales volume increased through expanded sales, expenses rose due to inflation and the impact of falling butadiene market prices, and a subsidiary in this segment recorded an impairment loss. The impairment loss for the period was ¥5,681 million. Segment assets were ¥319,009 million, the number of employees was 3,218, and capital expenditure was ¥16,397 million for construction work on elastomer-related facilities. For S-SBR (solution-polymerized styrene-butadiene rubber), a strategic product of the core elastomer business and a high-performance tire material, the company states that global demand continues to expand as a material supporting improved performance of next-generation tires and reduced environmental impact, and that it will further strengthen cooperation among Japan, Thailand, and Hungary in manufacturing to build a stable global supply system. In November 2025, the company decided to increase S-SBR production capacity by 10,000 tons at the Yokkaichi Plant, which handles research and development through to manufacturing in an integrated manner. In research and development, the company has developed a new-material theme generation AI agent system that integrates its proprietary knowledge graph with AI agent technology, and has started internal verification since October 2025.
entries.e8566c703bc2ffb8: Consolidated revenue in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥11,765,470 million, a decrease of 4.5% from the same period of the previous year. Revenue from external customers by segment is Petroleum Products and Other ¥10,341,787 million, Other ¥491,373 million, Functional Materials ¥336,507 million, Electricity ¥332,198 million, Oil and Natural Gas Exploration and Production ¥216,744 million, and Renewable Energy ¥46,861 million. Compared with the same period of the previous year (on a sales results basis), Electricity at 106.1%, Renewable Energy at 108.1%, and Other at 103.1% increased revenue, while Petroleum Products and Other at 94.9%, Functional Materials at 97.7%, and Oil and Natural Gas Exploration and Production at 89.3% decreased revenue. The main reasons for the decrease in revenue are Petroleum Products and Other and Oil and Natural Gas Exploration and Production, and in both cases falling crude oil and natural gas prices and the appreciation of the yen had an effect. The period average crude oil price (Dubai crude) was $72 for 1 barrel, $7 lower than the same period of the previous year, and the period average of the yen's exchange rate against the U.S. dollar was ¥151, with the yen appreciating by ¥2 from the same period of the previous year. Each segment's revenue includes intersegment internal revenue of ¥103,500 million in total (¥113,500 million in the same period of the previous year). Sales volume for Petroleum Products and Other increased by 2.7% from the same period of the previous year, because export volume increased in response to refinery operating conditions, despite a structural decline in domestic demand and the thorough pursuit of profitable sales. Note that care is needed in comparisons with the fiscal year ended March 2025 and earlier. With the new listing of JX Advanced Metals Corporation on March 19, 2025, the metals business was classified as a discontinued operation, and revenue from the fiscal year ended March 2024 onward is the amount for continuing operations only.
entries.e8de85324e04fb7f: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥466,627 million, up ¥360.5 billion year on year. Operating profit equivalent, excluding inventory effects (the effect on cost of sales of inventory valuation under the total average method and write-downs of inventory book value), was ¥474.4 billion, up ¥310.7 billion year on year. After deducting ¥17.8 billion, the net of finance income of ¥20,782 million and finance costs of ¥38,654 million, profit before tax was ¥448,755 million (up ¥360.6 billion year on year). After deducting income tax expense of ¥141.6 billion, profit for the year was ¥307.2 billion (up ¥20.3 billion year on year), of which profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥258,726 million and profit attributable to non-controlling interests was ¥48.5 billion. Segment profit (shown as operating profit in the consolidated statement of income) was ¥292,362 million for Petroleum Products and Others, ¥92,759 million for Other, ¥50,833 million for Oil and Natural Gas Development, ¥21,996 million for Electricity, ¥11,076 million for Functional Materials, −¥929 million for Renewable Energy, and −¥1,470 million for adjustments. The main driver of the profit increase was Petroleum Products and Others, which improved by ¥343.1 billion, from a loss of ¥50,705 million in the previous year to ¥292,362 million. The ¥92,759 million for Other includes equity-method investment income from the metals business, which consists of JX Metals and its subsidiaries and became an equity-method affiliate. Impairment losses on a consolidated basis were ¥48,011 million (¥197,806 million in the previous year), comprising ¥26,877 million for Petroleum Products and Others, ¥8,047 million for Electricity, ¥5,681 million for Functional Materials, ¥4,597 million for Oil and Natural Gas Development, ¥2,469 million for Renewable Energy, and ¥340 million for Other. As for financial position, total assets were ¥9,094,314 million (up ¥304.9 billion from the end of the previous consolidated fiscal year), total liabilities were ¥5.3361 trillion (up ¥17.3 billion), and total equity was ¥3.7582 trillion (up ¥287.6 billion). Interest-bearing debt (including lease liabilities) was ¥2.6157 trillion, down ¥60.3 billion from the end of the previous consolidated fiscal year, and net interest-bearing debt, after deducting cash on hand, was ¥1.7038 trillion, down ¥83.5 billion. Net cash provided by operating activities was an increase of ¥620.0 billion, net cash used in investing activities was a decrease of ¥252.0 billion, and net cash used in financing activities was a decrease of ¥361.0 billion. Cash and cash equivalents at the end of the fiscal year were ¥877.3 billion. To facilitate fund-raising and its global business, the company has obtained credit ratings from three agencies: Rating and Investment Information, Inc. (R&I), Japan Credit Rating Agency, Ltd. (JCR), and Moody's Japan. As of June 2026, its long-term ratings were AA- from R&I, AA- from JCR, and Baa2 from Moody's Japan (all with stable outlooks).

entries.f0d10bf17b4ec5e1: This is a reportable segment engaged in wind power, solar power and biomass power generation, carried out by ENEOS Renewable Energy Corporation. It is a company that became a subsidiary of the company after changing its trade name in April 2024 from Japan Renewable Energy Corporation. The company states that it develops, generates and sells power from renewable energy sources such as solar, onshore wind and biomass, and that it aims in future to broadly cover renewable energy as a whole, including offshore wind. Sales to external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥46,861 million, the smallest among the reportable segments; sales including inter-segment sales were ¥48,657 million (up 10.7% from the same period of the previous year), and the segment loss was ¥929 million (a loss of ¥16,906 million in the same period of the previous year). The company explains that, although it recorded impairment losses and other items accompanying the cancellation of development of some projects, profit increased because power generation rose with the start of operation of new solar and onshore wind power plants. Impairment losses for the fiscal year were ¥2,469 million. Segment assets were ¥583,062 million, and the fact that assets are more than 12 times external sales of ¥46,861 million is a characteristic of a business that owns power generation facilities. The number of employees was 569, and capital expenditure was ¥26,823 million for construction of renewable energy power source facilities. In the fiscal year, it started operation of a total of 14 wind and solar power plants, and, to reduce the risk of output curtailment and aim for a stable supply of renewable energy, it promoted installing storage batteries at solar power plants and started operation at a total of 5 locations. The power generation capacity according to its equity stake as of March 31, 2026 (excluding sources under construction) is about 1,300,000 kW. It also worked to improve power generation through more advanced remote monitoring to raise plant utilization rates and through repowering of plants with significant equipment deterioration.
